stem: On a tea estate near Sylhet, Bangladesh, the rows of tea bushes are straight and parallel. A straight footpath crosses two of the rows, as shown, making a \(118^{\circ}\) angle with the first row. What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: The two rows are parallel lines, and the footpath is a transversal.
The \(118^{\circ}\) angle and the \(x^{\circ}\) angle are in the same position at the two crossings, so they are corresponding angles.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 118\); corresponding angles are equal, not supplementary.
explanation.B: Correct. The two angles are corresponding angles at parallel lines, so \(x = 118\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(118 - 90\); there is no right angle in the figure to subtract from.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is half of 118; a parallel-line angle pair is equal or supplementary, never halved.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['U'][1]==P['V'][1] and P['J'][1]==P['K'][1]
assert abs(ang('U','E','F')-118)<0.1 and abs(ang('J','F','H')-118)<0.1
ans=118
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
